qs.q: What does the attribute `method` do in the `<form>` tag?

c.x: To identify the way (HTTP method) the data is sent
To identify the PHP file that the data will be sent to
To open the form in another window

qs.e: The `method` attribute indicates which HTTP method (`get` or `post`) is used to get the form data to the server. The page that handles the data is given by `action`, and checking the inputs before sending is the job of `onsubmit`.

qs.q: Which tag is used to create a text area in an HTML form?
qs.e: A multi-line text box is made with `<textarea name="" rows="" cols="">` ... `</textarea>`. `<input type="text">` creates only a single-line text box, and `<text>` and `type="textarea"` do not exist.

qs.q: Which tag creates a check box in an HTML form?
qs.e: Check boxes are created with the `<input>` element and `type="checkbox"` (used when multiple selections are allowed). The other forms are not valid HTML syntax.

qs.q: Which HTML tag is used to define an internal style sheet?
qs.e: An embedded (internal) style sheet is written between `<style>` ... `</style>` inside the `<head>` section of the page. `<link>` references an external file, `<script>` holds scripts and `<css>` does not exist.

qs.q: Which element is used in the `<head>` section if we want to use an external style sheet file to decorate the page?
qs.e: An external style sheet is attached with `<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="1.css" />` placed in the `<head>`. `<style>` is for embedded rules, `href` is only an attribute of `<link>`, and `<title>` sets the page title.
qs.ref: Lecture 3 - Linking to an External CSS

qs.q: Which of the following is the correct syntax for referring to an external style sheet?
qs.e: The CSS rules are saved in a `.css` file and referenced from the `<head>` of each HTML page with the `<link>` tag, using `rel="stylesheet"`, `type="text/css"` and `href` for the file name. The other tags do not exist or do not load a style file.
qs.ref: Lecture 3 - Linking to an External CSS

qs.q: In CSS, how do you select an element with the class name `demo`?
qs.e: Class selectors are identified by the dot (.) symbol, so `.demo` selects elements with `class="demo"`. The hash (#) symbol is for ID selectors, and `demo` alone would select an HTML element named demo.

qs.q: If we want to define a style for a unique element, which CSS selector will be used?
qs.e: An ID selector (identified by #) is meant for one unique element, because an id value identifies a single element in the page. Class selectors (.) can be applied to many elements.

qs.q: Which attribute is used to name an element uniquely?
qs.e: The `id` attribute gives an element a unique identifier, and it is what an ID selector (`#name`) refers to. The `class` attribute can be shared by many elements.

qs.q: To ______ selectors, separate each selector with a comma.
qs.e: A comma lets one CSS rule apply to several elements, e.g. `h1, h2, h3 { color: #000000; }`; this is called grouping selectors. Each property inside the rule is separated by a semicolon.

qs.q: A CSS style rule is made up of:

c.x: a selector and a declaration (property : value)
an HTML tag and an attribute

qs.e: A rule has two basic parts: the selector (what to modify) and the declaration (how to modify it). The declaration itself has two parts, a property and a value, as in `h2 { font-style : italic }`.

qs.q: How do you make all paragraph elements red in color?
qs.e: An HTML selector uses the tag name without brackets, so `p {color: red;}` styles every paragraph. `p.all` selects only paragraphs with class `all`, and `all.p` is not a valid selector for all paragraphs.

qs.q:
What is the correct CSS syntax for making all the `

` elements bold?
qs.e: The bold property is `font-weight`, and a rule with an HTML selector `p` applies to all paragraphs. `text-size` is not a CSS property, `font-size` controls size and not boldness, and the inline versions would affect only one paragraph.

qs.q: Which CSS property is used to control the text size of an element?
qs.e: `font-size` sets the size of the text and is one of the font properties in the lecture. `font-style` sets italic or normal, and `text-size` and `text-style` are not CSS properties.

qs.q: How do you change the text color of an element in CSS?
qs.e: The `color` property sets the text color, written as `property : value` such as `color : blue`. `text-color` and `fgcolor` are not CSS properties.

qs.q: Which of the following properties specifies the color of a border?
qs.e: `border-color` is one of the border properties (with `border-style` and `border-width`). `border-style` sets the line type, and `color-border` and `style-border` do not exist.

qs.q: Which CSS property is used to change the background color of an element?
qs.e: `background-color` is the CSS property for the background color. `color` changes the text color, and `bgcolor` is an old HTML attribute, not a CSS property.

qs.q: Which of the following CSS properties is used to set the background image of an element?
qs.e: `background-image` is the CSS property that sets an image as the background of an element, and it is listed with the color and background properties in the lecture. `background-color` sets a plain color.

qs.q: Which of the following is the correct syntax to make the background color of all paragraphs yellow?
qs.e: Use the HTML selector `p` with the `background-color` property. A `#` must be followed by a hex code, so `#yellow` is invalid, and `all` is not a valid selector.

qs.q: What is the preferred way of adding a background color in HTML?
qs.e: Styling is done with CSS, here as an inline style: `style="property : value"` on the tag. `background` on the body expects an image file (not a color), and `<background>` is not an HTML tag.

qs.q: Which of the following syntaxes is correct in CSS to make each word of a sentence start with a capital letter?
qs.e: `text-transform` is one of the text properties, and its value `capitalize` makes the first letter of each word a capital letter. `uppercase` would turn all letters into capitals, and `text-style` and `transform` are not the right properties.
